response.rationale: R6 (Giant Cell Tumor) best matches the imaging features: soap-bubble appearance, cortical destruction, and soft-tissue component (implied by avid enhancement). R5 (Eosinophilic Granuloma) also has soap-bubble but lacks cortical destruction and is more common in children. The patient's age of 50 and painless presentation are more consistent with GCT than EG.

rejected.why: Brown tumor requires hyperparathyroidism, but labs are unremarkable.
Fibrous dysplasia typically has ground-glass appearance, not soap-bubble.
Ewing's sarcoma is more common in younger patients and typically has onion-skin periosteal reaction, not soap-bubble.
